subject: Proposed controls for on-prem deployment — license boundaries & escrow
messages:
From: Michael Sanders <michael.sanders@medsysinc.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@medsysinc.com
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Controls for on-prem deployment — escrow and audits

Evelyn,

Thanks for the demo last week. As we move into legal review for the on-prem deployment, Procurement and Legal have flagged two items that will block our PO unless addressed in the MSA/Order Form addenda:

1) An escrow-like mechanism (source + build artifacts) that can be released to MedSys if Redwood fails to support the product or ceases business;
2) Clear, contractual audit rights (including the right to engage a third-party auditor) to validate data separation and key custody for the deployed instance.

We understand standard options vary — source escrow, escrow plus attestations, or ongoing evidence packages. Procurement asked for a short proposal outlining the possible approaches and the tradeoffs (time/cost/ops). Also include any limitations on on-site audits and how you handle cryptographic keys.

Attached is our internal audit guide for reference (MedSys_Audit_Guidelines.pdf). Would appreciate an initial redline on the MSA and a suggested Order Form clause set we can share with Legal.

Best,
Michael Sanders
Sr. Counsel, MedSys Inc
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Michael Sanders <michael.sanders@medsysinc.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Controls for on-prem deployment — escrow and audits

Michael —

Thanks for the clear summary. I'm looping in Karthik (sales) and Marcus (security/compliance) so we can propose a pragmatic path that balances MedSys's procurement requirements with Redwood's operational constraints. High-level options we'll propose:

- Option A: Source + deterministic build artifacts placed into a neutral escrow agent; release trigger is vendor insolvency or sustained failure to support per SLA. Escrow content limited to narrowly scoped components required to build the runtime (not internal infra tooling).
- Option B: Annual third-party attestation (SOC2 + targeted deployment attestation) combined with a live evidence package (audit logs, KMS attestations, build hashes) delivered on request; limited on-site audits with 30-day notice.
- Option C: Encrypted key-share escrow (split keys with HSM) — we hold operational key shares, MedSys holds backup shares with escrow agent; release only under pre-agreed conditions.

I'm attaching a first-pass redline for the MSA clauses and an Exhibit A that documents proposed deployment boundaries (Redline_MSA_escrow_v1.docx, Exhibit-A-deployment-boundaries.pdf).

A few clarifying Qs for Legal/Procurement to help us sharpen the draft:
- Are you expecting unilateral auditor appointment or a mutually agreeable list of auditors?
- Preferred frequency for on-site audits (annual vs. biennial)?
- Any regulatory constraints that require source escrow vs. attestation?

We'll aim to get a consolidated suggested language back by EOD Thursday (Nov 26) so you have something to circulate internally.

Regards,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Contracts Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Michael Sanders <michael.sanders@medsysinc.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@medsysinc.com, Lisa Cox <lisa.cox@medsysinc.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 08:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Controls for on-prem deployment — escrow and audits

Evelyn —

Thanks for the quick response. A few clarifications from our side:

- Procurement prefers the ability to appoint a third-party auditor from an approved list without Redwood's veto, but Legal may accept a mutually agreed list if you provide names.
- For our risk profile, an on-site audit once every 24 months is sufficient, with remote evidence requests allowed in between.
- Regarding keys: we need technical detail on how keys are created, where they are stored (HSM vs. software), and whether Redwood or MedSys holds escrow copies.

We're not asking for full source access today, but we need contract language that allows for a narrowly scoped release under defined triggers. Attached is our procurement team's template language and audit guidelines (MedSys_Audit_Guidelines.pdf).

If you can reflect the auditor appointment language and the 24-month cadence in your draft, Legal will be able to take a first pass.

Best,
Michael
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Michael Sanders <michael.sanders@medsysinc.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 10:21:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Controls for on-prem deployment — escrow and audits

Michael, team —

Thanks for the detail. From a security/compliance standpoint we can accommodate a practical middle ground. Key recommendations:

- Auditor appointment: Accept a mutually-agreed list of reputable auditors (we can provide names: NCC Group, Coalfire, Schellman). If MedSys insists on unilateral appointment, we need a defined conflicts process and a requirement that the auditor has Redwood confidentiality & AUP terms.

- Audit cadence: Accept biennial on-site audits (every 24 months) with a 30-day notice period. Remote evidence requests (logs, KMS attestations, build hashes) can be provided within 10 business days for routine checks.

- Escrow approach: Preferred model is a hybrid: store deterministic build artifacts + cryptographic hashes in an escrow with a neutral agent; sensitive signing keys remain in a Redwood-managed HSM. For emergency recoveries we can store an encrypted split-key with the escrow agent (multi-party threshold scheme). Release conditions must be explicitly limited to vendor insolvency or prolonged SLA breach (>60 days) and require an independent verification step.

- Operational controls: We will supply a deployment evidence package (build manifests, container hashes, provenance logs, KMS attestation reports) as part of each attestation. On-site audits may not include access to Redwood internal developer workstations or non-customer-specific telemetry.

Attached: Escrow_Spec_v3.pdf (details on artifacts, retention, encryption).

If that sounds acceptable, Legal (Laura/Evelyn) can draft the final MSA redlines referencing these constraints.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Director, Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Michael Sanders <michael.sanders@medsysinc.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2026 15:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Controls for on-prem deployment — escrow and audits

Michael —

Appreciate the quick collaboration here. We believe Marcus's hybrid approach hits the sweet spot:

- MedSys gets strong recoverability guarantees via escrowed artifacts and clearly defined release triggers;
- MedSys retains the right to auditing under the mutually-agreed auditor framework (we'll share a vendor list immediately);
- Operational impact to Redwood is minimized by limiting on-site scope and preserving HSM-controlled keys.

Next steps I propose:
1) Laura & Evelyn to incorporate Marcus's language into a redline MSA + Order Form (Evelyn: can you please post updated redline by EOD Tuesday Nov 30?).
2) I'll follow up in HubSpot and include an optional commercial concession (one-time onboarding credit) if MedSys accepts the attestation + escrow model rather than full source escrow.
3) DocuSign link & final Order Form will be issued after Legal confirms redline.

I've attached the current Order Form draft (OrderForm_Draft_001.pdf). If procurement is comfortable with the attestation + escrow proposal, we can fast-track signatures.

Thanks — looking forward to wrapping this up.

Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
